_readme: What both roads out of the village say before Rook is along. The keep's gate wants a KEY,
which is a fetch; this one wants a PERSON, which is a decision - so the refusal names her
and where she is, and a player who walks west first leaves with a lead rather than a wall.
It exists because M29 sized every fight for two. The genre's own answer is to put the
second sword on the critical path - Dragon Quest II hands you the Prince through the
story - and a companion the player may decline turns one design into two, of which only
one was ever balanced. Rook's own line already argued it: two of us come back from it.
The warden speaks, because she is the one who said one sword was enough for a village this
size, and this is that line being wrong out loud.

refused.speaker: Warden
refused.text: Not alone you don't. I said one sword was enough for this village - the road is not this village. Rook is down by the west wall.

wait.speaker: Warden
wait.text: Take her, and I will open it myself.
